questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture and that it was inside EU

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, KU Leuven was extremly good at welcoming new exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A whole week full of introduction courses and studen network events (ESN events).
The voluntary Erasmus Student Network was sublime!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: You feel very informed and welcome!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think i was pretty lucky and found my own pretty quickly on Facebook

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Begin the process of searching for housing early!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not enough cheap alternatives

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Very easy and intuitive 
So satisfying that you were able to change courses after they had started, that way you had the opportunity to try the course first and then maybe change course afterwards.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had a portal where you could pick the courses, and then you could change courses until two weeks after the beginning of the semester

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Their student counsler, Kathleen Monsieur was especially helpful and kind,  and the student office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to pick what they think sounds interesting, they can always change their decision later on

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The available courses for bachelor students on the Business and economics faculty was very limited and rather unilateral.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was decent but all my courses on the Business and economics faculty was closed book multiple-choice exams, where wrong answers had a negative score, which is the most demotivating and unfulfilling way to do an exam! Horrible to be honest

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH is way better in the form that it is less formal, you actually get asked questions and dare to aske them your self. The level of the teaching is similar but the quality of the teaching is better at UCPH at least in the courses i had.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Business Information Systems (D0H27A)
Consumer Behaviour (D0R13A)
Principles of Database Management (D0I62A)
Russia and Eurasia in the Global Context (S0I67A)
Supply Chain Management (D0R17A)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Russia and Eurasia in the Global Context (S0I67A) is probably the best course i have ever had, not only because of the current situation with the war in Ukraine but also just in general. They way the teaching is carried out is sublime and the interaction with the students are great, especially due to the large number of different nationalities in the class.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Laundry! 
There are no washing machines in the student housing, so you have to use laundromats, which are really expensive, approximately 150 kr. for two washes and drying.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Going out to eat and drink was cheaper 
Food in supermarkets was also a bit cheaper than DK
Otherwise the prices were pretty similar to danish prices

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Never have i seen so good sport facilities! They were truly legendary, almost worthy of American College athletes. And all of it is free for exchange students! except the fitness, but it was still really cheap and better than any public fitness center i Denmark.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They had student teams within every thinkable sport and athletic discipline. 
As a student you can buy a culture card which grand you free access to a lot of cultural events and institution and the few things that are not free are heavily discounted for students. 
Their Erasmus Student Network was simply amazing, they have a whole building just dedicated to exchange students, where they can hang out and drink coffee and get to know other exchange students, they also facilitate multiple events throughout the semester even weekend trips. 
The faculties also offer a lot of social events and activities. Over all very impress how committed the local students are in the social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
You have to try a Cantus, it is an experience you will never forget! 
Also really take advantage of the sports facilities, especially the indoor beach-volley courts

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit Ghent and Brugge 
And take advantage of the planned trips from ESN

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, they are almost more Danish than Danish people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to a Cantus!
Also dont be afraid to initiate the contact, they are very much alike the danish students, they don't initiate the contact but when someone else does they are very open and friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The age gap, the bachelor students are very young and still quite dependent on their parents, so dependent that they go home every weekend to get their cloths washed and get new food for the fridge

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Probably their friendliness and their love for beer

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared on studying a lot more than you are used to
Take advantage of all the offers the university has 
Drink a lot of beer

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to study a lot, they expect a lot more than UCPH pr. ects point 
It is a really hardcore student environment, people study a lot and you are expected to do the same. So if you want to have an easy semester you should pick another university! Really!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The people i got to meet, and alle the new cultures i got to know. 
It is a really unique way to get to meet new people from all around the world (mainly Europe)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
You are very much on your own the first couple of months, before you get to know people. 
The new way of studying is also quite a challenge

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
